**Finding: COMPLIANT (preferred position met) — no redline proposed.**

The NONCOMPETE rule's preferred position is the *absence* of any restraint on our business, and that is what this Agreement delivers.

**What I checked and why each candidate is not a Customer non-compete:**

| Location | Text | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| p1490–p1491 (Confidentiality attachment) | Recipient not precluded from "providing to others products or services which may be competitive with products or services of the Discloser" | Affirmative freedom-to-compete; runs in our favour |
| p0116 (§ 5.1(b)(v)) | Termination trigger where a Party is acquired by an entity that competes directly with the other | Mutual change-of-control termination right, not a restraint on what IBM may build, buy or sell |
| p0995 (§ 14.18 "Restrictions and Limitations") | Limits MSL's use of IBM property and other performance obligations | Binds **MSL**; benefits us — not flagged |
| p0767–p0775 (Attachment 1, § 7.4) | Redacted disclosure / right-to-match mechanic | Expressly permits IBM to move the Product to the third party if MSL cannot match. Per the rule boundary, a right-to-match mechanic is MFN territory and is not exclusivity absent an outright prohibition on using alternatives — deliberately not double-flagged here |
| p0197–p0198 (§ 13.0 IP) | IBM owns Product IP; MSL restricted from proprietary processes | No field-of-use limit on IBM |

Targeted searches for "compete", "exclusive", field-of-use/territory, "sole source"/"all of its requirements", "covenant not to", "prohibited from", and "IBM shall not / agrees not to" produced no covenant binding IBM.

Because the preferred element — *"Customer has no non-compete or field-of-use restriction"* — is satisfied on the face of the document, there is nothing to narrow to the fallback and no walk-away exposure (no post-term restraint, no undefined "any competing business" scope). I did not propose a redline, consistent with the instruction not to flag terms that benefit our party.
